scope: Three missing Weatherman activists discovered during Panther-support research, with four distinct custody cases; no claim of formal Black Panther membership.

release1969.label: Jeff Magalif, The Harvard Crimson, October 30, 1969: Mann, Weathermen Released After Arrests for Disruptions. Detailed arrest, overnight release, recommitment and four-day jail chronology.

english_verdict.label: Jeff Magalif, The Harvard Crimson, November 8, 1969: Judge Convicts Mann On Charge of Assault. November 7 misdemeanor verdicts, concurrent sentences, appeal and release on bond.

cfia_sentence.label: Jeff Magalif, The Harvard Crimson, January 26, 1970: Mann Gets Another Year For Role in CFIA Attack. Friday January 23 sentence and immediate commencement of imprisonment.

cfia_custody.label: Jeremy S. Bluhm, The Harvard Crimson, March 26, 1970: Police Make a New Arrest In CFIA Disruption Case. Mann still imprisoned; anti-imperialist political context of the violent raid.

mann_appeal.label: Eric M. Mann v. Commonwealth, 359 Mass. 661, decided June 15, 1971. Judicial opinion upholding sentence after de novo Superior Court trial.

mann_memoir.label: Eric Mann, Comrade George (1972), printed pages 1 and 5, PDF pages 3 and 5. First-person account of a year and a half in prison and the final nine months at Concord; opening scene places him free in Berkeley after George Jackson’s death in August 1971.

mann_birth.label: Eric Mann, Palestine Will Win, CounterPunch, September 3, 2014. First-person statement that he was born in Brooklyn in 1942; no month or day provided.

usc_profile.label: Manuel Pastor and Michele Prichard, L.A. Rising (USC, 2012), printed page 78 / PDF page 79. Eric Mann interview profile and explicitly identified embedded portrait.

school_context.label: Kirkpatrick Sale, SDS (1973), printed page 420 / PDF page 422. Places Boston English High School in the Weatherman school confrontation/recruitment campaign before the Chicago National Action. Historical synthesis, used only for campaign context.

boston_map.label: U.S. Department of Transportation ITS Deployment Evaluation: Boston city coordinates. Used only for an approximate historical case-city marker.

prisoner.name: Eric M. Mann
prisoner.description: Eric M. Mann, born in Brooklyn in 1942, was a civil-rights and antiwar organizer associated with CORE, SDS and the Weathermen. His Boston English High School case involved four days of pretrial custody and an appealed misdemeanor conviction. In a separate case, he was imprisoned for assault and battery during the September 1969 attack on Harvard’s Center for International Affairs, a target of anti-imperialist protest. He later described serving a year and a half, including nine months at Concord. After prison, he wrote about George Jackson and continued organizing; he helped establish the Labor/Community Strategy Center in Los Angeles.

research_notes: Preserve every existing identity and all populated fields. Boston coordinates are approximate historical case-city markers. Only year precision is known for Mann’s birth and prison release. Imposed three-month and two-year terms are not substituted for actual custody. No news source in personal support website fields.
